style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression down a data hall rack row; a single GPU accelerator blade is pulled partway out of its brushed-steel bay at lower-right third, copper heat fins catching a low raking shaft of late-day sun from the left with hard directional falloff, while identical racks recede into deep charcoal shadow. Palette graphite, cobalt, bone white; brushed steel, copper heat pipes, perforated metal. Extreme asymmetry, long-lens stacked layers, crisp high-contrast air, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI labels, illegible characters
rationale: This story is about scale and a cost collapse across compute supply: a compressed 200mm long-lens view of a data hall communicates the industrial abundance of token-generating hardware, while the single pulled blade foregrounds the price/capacity mechanism without lapsing into a generic datacenter wide shot.
subject: a single GPU accelerator blade pulled partway from a brushed-steel rack bay
core_thesis: A daily dollar budget is written in the one input whose price is falling fastest, so Apple's cut from $300 to $200 still raises the tokens each engineer can buy by about 2.85 times.
core_conflict: fixed-dollar caps versus rapidly falling token unit prices; a tighter ceiling can still loosen effective token supply.
composition: extreme asymmetry with 200mm telephoto compression; one lit blade at lower-right third, rows receding left

review.depicts: A single GPU accelerator blade with a copper heat-pipe shroud sits partway out of a brushed-steel server rack bay on the right, with parallel rows of perforated rack panels receding into soft focus to the left.
review.reason: The article's mechanism is the price of AI compute, and a partly withdrawn accelerator blade in a rack is the literal hardware that sets that token price, so a reader would connect the frame to the story.
